name: min_total_chars-inclusive-boundary
note: A 25-byte assistant turn plus a 15-byte user turn totals exactly 40 bytes; min_total_chars:40 is inclusive (>=), so it matches even though the 15-byte routing input is far below the bound.

name: min_total_chars-below-boundary
note: One byte short of the bound: 24 + 15 = 39 bytes misses min_total_chars:40, is above max_total_chars:6, and the 15-byte routing input misses min_chars:40, so it falls through to default.

name: max_total_chars-inclusive-boundary
note: A single 6-byte message totals 6 bytes; max_total_chars:6 is inclusive (<=), so it matches.

name: total_chars-utf8-byte-count
note: Each 'é' is 1 character but 2 UTF-8 bytes, so 'éééé' totals 8 bytes. 8 misses max_total_chars:6 -> default (local); counting characters (4 <= 6) would match -> cloud. Routing to local proves the total is measured in bytes, not characters.

name: long-history-short-last-turn
note: The motivating case: 102 bytes of history ending in a 5-byte 'go on'. min_total_chars:40 matches on the conversation while min_chars:40 cannot see past the final turn. Were the total measured on the routing input alone it would read 5 bytes and this request would instead match max_total_chars:6, so matched_rule discriminates the two implementations.

messages.content: Explain how a B-tree index works.
A B-tree keeps keys sorted in nodes.

name: total_chars-counts-every-role
note: system 14 + user 15 + assistant 11 + tool 11 = 51 bytes, no single message reaching 40. Counting only user turns would total 15 and fall through to default, so matching min_total_chars:40 proves every role counts.

name: prompt-form-total-equals-chars
note: A legacy completions prompt carries no history, so its total equals the routing input: 40 bytes matches min_total_chars:40. A total that ignored the prompt form would leave min_chars:40 to match instead, changing matched_rule.

name: responses-input-array-sums-all-items
note: Responses `input` array: a 25-byte assistant item plus a 15-byte user item totals 40. Counting only the last user item would total 15 and fall through to default.

name: min_total_chars-trace
note: route_trace:true records the matching leaf under condition 'min_total_chars', not the 'min_chars' it shares an implementation with.

name: max_total_chars-trace
note: Both earlier rules miss (traced false under their own condition names), then max_total_chars-rule matches under condition 'max_total_chars'.
